hypothesis: An acknowledged scorer sample can be joined to a positive scorer event and then to one admitted owner key occurrence only when sample/update identity, run identity, action binding, and release bounds are all present and consistent.
test: Generate two deterministic samples through the frozen AcknowledgedSampler with a fake game, feed them to the frozen ProgressClock, and compose one positive event through the frozen occurrence reducer. Exercise cross-run, missing producer, misclocked event, repeated sequence, terminal mutation, and release-sync-boundary controls.

decision.pass: The exact event maps to its unique acknowledged sample and the one matching occurrence is returned as unique_temporal_occurrence; all mismatched or incomplete identity controls fail closed, and release-bracket events remain unresolved.
decision.fail: Any mismatched producer/action run is joined, any event without an exact acknowledged sample is attributed, or a release-boundary event becomes active.
decision.scope: Deterministic synthetic source-composition construction only. No actual engine, V16 session, X11 server, controller, model, game allocation, task effect, or physical input.

competing_explanation: Numeric clock overlap alone may appear sufficient; cross-run controls test whether that would create a false join.
uncertainty: The owner occurrence candidate does not yet emit the scorer run_id in its admission/release records, so the same-run binding tested here is a required source contract, not demonstrated live telemetry. Producer freshness and clocks are also not qualified against an actual engine session.
host: Windows host / Python 3.13 and Ubuntu WSL / Python 3.12; WSLc executable unavailable
